predecessors.name: Principality of Moldavia
predecessors.text: the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia between the Prut and the Dniester

predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Budjak, where the Ottomans ruled directly

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: Bessarabia stays Russian: an oblast from 1818 and a guberniya from 1873

ledger.x: 28 May 1812: the Treaty of Bucharest cedes Bessarabia to Russia.
28 May 1812: the Budjak passes from the Ottomans to Russia, 'ceded by the Ottoman Empire (to which Moldavia was a vassal) to Russia'.
Cliopatria's row ends in 1813 and Cliopatria's Russian Empire shape covers the land throughout; the page is silent on any 1813 event.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) concluded the war: the Ottoman Empire ceded the land between the Pruth and the Dniester to Russia, 'That entire region was then called Bessarabia.'

certainty.note: The pages give the Prut and Dniester as the limits of the ceded land but no surveyed line in the south (Danube mouths, Black Sea coast) or around Khotyn.
